references.text: God's command regarding the covenant of circumcision, which Abraham immediately obeys in verse 23 by circumcising every male in his household.
Abraham circumcised his son Isaac when he was eight days old, in obedience to the same covenant command he followed in Genesis 17:23.
Stephen refers to the covenant of circumcision that God gave Abraham and how Abraham circumcised Isaac—a testimony to Abraham's obedience to God's covenant command.
Paul explains that Abraham's circumcision was a sign and seal of the righteousness he had already received by faith, giving theological depth to the act of circumcision in Genesis 17:23.
Connects Ishmael's birth and naming (Genesis 16:15) with his inclusion in the covenant through circumcision (Genesis 17:23), showing Abraham's obedience toward all the men in his household.
Genesis 17:23 is the concrete action that fulfills the principle in Genesis 18:19 about charging the household to keep to the Lord's way.

Creates a narrative contrast: Ishmael is included in the covenant through circumcision (Genesis 17:23) but is later sent away from the inheritance (Genesis 25:6), highlighting the dividing line between the covenant and the special son of promise.
